canonical_unit_note: 50 kg bag. Also priced per tonne at 20 bags/tonne — the price filter bands on ₹/bag delivered, never on ₹/tonne, or a jumbo bag and a 50 kg bag land in the same band.
counts_note: Counts measured from data/buildobjects.db on 2026-08-05 for hyderabad. Each count is a number of OFFERS, not products: the results list shows one card per vendor, so the rail counts sellers' listings and these numbers match it exactly. A facet marked data_backed:false has no field behind it in the collected data and ships disabled with a reason.
lead_reason: OPC and PPC are not substitutes — the buyer's job (slab vs plaster) decides the chemistry before anything else does, and it eliminates more of the catalogue than any other single choice.

filters.label: Type
filters.why: The genuine first decision. PPC is fly-ash blended and slower-setting; OPC 53 is the slab cement. Choosing wrong costs strength or money.

filters.label: Grade
filters.why: Only OPC carries a grade in this sense. Showing an empty grade filter on a PPC listing is the classic flat-panel mistake.
filters.note: IS 269:2015 consolidated the older grade-specific standards IS 8112 (43) and IS 12269 (53) into one.

filters.label: Brand
filters.why: Brand sits above price here, against the usual order. Cement is the most brand-loyal category in Indian construction and a large share of buyers start with the name, not the spec.

filters.label: Pack size
filters.why: Bulk changes the entire price basis. A 1 MT jumbo and a 50 kg bag in one price band is the basis error this engine exists to remove.

filters.label: Order quantity
filters.why: A contractor and a homeowner are different buyers on the same page. Selecting the slab shows the price that actually applies instead of making them compute it per card.
filters.no_data_reason: No collected listing in hyderabad populates `offer.bulk_slabs`. The facet is retained and shipped disabled rather than deleted, so the gap is visible rather than silently absent.

filters.label: BIS licence
filters.why: Cement is covered by a quality-control order that makes a valid BIS licence a legal condition of sale — so this is not a preference. But almost no listing publishes the licence number, and 'not published by this seller' is a different claim from 'not licensed'.
filters.note: Default off. Three honest states, never collapsed into a pass/fail.
filters.needs_verification: The Cement (Quality Control) Order 2003, S.O. 191(E) dated 17 Feb 2003 is named in a secondary source (spec §D8.1a) and has not been read against the gazette. The QCO hard filter in this build fires only on positive evidence of an EXPIRED licence, never on a listing that simply does not quote one — see the demo-simplification note in the production prompt.

values.label: BIS-licensed brand, licence not quoted
values.sublabel: manufacturer holds a licence; this listing does not publish it

filters.label: Arrives
filters.why: Computed per pincode, not stored on the product — the same SKU is 'tomorrow' in Kukatpally and 'within a week' in a district town, so this facet cannot be cached without the pincode in the key.
filters.note: Scheduled delivery carries equal weight here. Construction buys are staged — cement at footing stage, months before finishing — so a chosen date is often the preferred option, not a lesser one.

filters.label: Application
filters.why: Many buyers shop by job rather than by chemistry. Folded rather than primary because it substantially restates Type once Type is chosen.
filters.no_data_reason: `attrs.application` is populated on 160 of 720 listings in hyderabad, but as uncontrolled seller text ("Construction Use", "Construction, Masonry Work, Plastering", "For Asbestos Pipes, RCC Beams And  RCC S") which matches none of this filter's values. The gap is normalisation, not collection: shipped disabled rather than deleted, and rather than mapped by guess.

filters.label: IS standard
filters.why: Professional buyers specify by IS code. Folded because the standard is fully implied by Type for most of the catalogue.

filters.label: Seller quotes price
filters.why: Not a filter any competitor offers. A GSTIN holder claiming input credit needs to know which sellers quote ex-GST; ranking is always on the landed figure regardless of what the seller quoted.

filters.label: Price verified
filters.why: Kept quiet and available rather than prominent. Most buyers will not touch it; the professional buyer who does will notice immediately that no competitor timestamps a price at all.
filters.note: Cement is volatility class V0 — a 24 h SLA, because the market moved ₹15–20/bag in one month.
filters.no_data_reason: No collected listing in hyderabad populates `price_current.freshness_state`. The facet is retained and shipped disabled rather than deleted, so the gap is visible rather than silently absent.

filters.label: Country of origin
filters.why: Built as a proper indexed, sortable facet rather than page text because LMPC Rule 6(10A) (G.S.R. 128(E), compliance date moved to 2027-07-01) requires origin to be searchable and sortable, and a text field cannot satisfy that.

omitted.reason: Moved to a toggle above the results rather than a rail block — it is a single binary and the rail slot is worth more to a spec filter. Default on, one click to undo.
Grey in every OPC/PPC/PSC listing; white cement is already its own Type value. One meaningful value is noise.
Held back until there is a real ratings corpus. B2B directory listings carry sparse ratings, and a filter that returns nothing makes the marketplace look empty.
Cement strike-through pricing in this market is computed against an inflated reference. A discount facet built on a manufactured number is worse than none.
